### Health Analytics with R · Module 03: Statistical Inference
***
**Learning objectives**
- Fit and interpret logistic regression for binary outcomes (readmission, mortality)
- Report adjusted ORs with 95% CIs from model output
- Assess model fit: Hosmer-Lemeshow test, calibration plot, ROC-AUC
- Detect and handle multicollinearity (VIF)
- Build a multivariable risk score with predicted probabilities

**Estimated time:** 2.5 hours | **Level:** Intermediate → Advanced | **Libraries:** `stats`, `broom`, `ggplot2`, `pROC`, `dplyr`

## 1. Setup & Dataset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(pROC)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod03_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod03")
dir.create(mod03_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

set.seed(42)
N <- 2000
base <- matrix(rnorm(N * 3), ncol = 3)

set.seed(99)
ages          <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes         <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers        <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03)
)
diabetes      <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.6 * base[, 1] - 0.5))
heart_failure <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * base[, 2] - 1.2))
copd          <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 3] - 1.0))
hypertension  <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.7 * base[, 1] - 0.2))
los_days      <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
admit_type    <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent"), N, replace = TRUE,
                        prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.18))
n_comorb      <- diabetes + heart_failure + copd + hypertension

readmit_logit <- (-3.0 + 0.7 * heart_failure + 0.5 * diabetes + 0.4 * copd
                  + 0.02 * (ages - 60) + 0.3 * as.integer(admit_type == "Emergency")
                  + 0.2 * as.integer(los_days > 7) + 0.3 * as.integer(payers == "Medicaid")
                  + rnorm(N, 0, 0.3))
readmitted_30 <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(readmit_logit))

df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = relevel(factor(payers), ref = "Private"),
  admit_type    = relevel(factor(admit_type), ref = "Elective"),
  los_days      = los_days,
  los_gt7       = as.integer(los_days > 7),
  diabetes      = diabetes,
  heart_failure = heart_failure,
  copd          = copd,
  hypertension  = hypertension,
  n_comorb      = n_comorb,
  readmitted_30 = readmitted_30
) |>
  mutate(age_std = as.numeric(scale(age)))

cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
```

## 2. Unadjusted (Univariable) Logistic Regression


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Run univariable logistic regression for each predictor
predictors <- list(
  c("heart_failure", "Heart failure"),
  c("diabetes", "Diabetes"),
  c("copd", "COPD"),
  c("hypertension", "Hypertension"),
  c("los_gt7", "LOS > 7 days"),
  c("age", "Age (per year)")
)

univar_results <- bind_rows(lapply(predictors, function(pair) {
  var <- pair[[1]]; label <- pair[[2]]
  model_u <- glm(as.formula(paste("readmitted_30 ~", var)), data = df, family = binomial())
  tid <- broom::tidy(model_u, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) |>
    filter(term == var)
  tibble(
    Predictor    = label,
    OR           = round(tid$estimate, 2),
    OR_lo        = round(tid$conf.low, 2),
    OR_hi        = round(tid$conf.high, 2),
    `p-value`    = round(tid$p.value, 4),
    Significant  = tid$p.value < 0.05
  )
}))

cat("Univariable logistic regression — Unadjusted OR (95% CI):\n")
```

## 4. Multicollinearity — Variance Inflation Factor


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# VIF for continuous and binary predictors
vif_from_lm <- function(data, vars) {
  X <- data[, vars, drop = FALSE]
  vapply(vars, function(v) {
    others <- setdiff(vars, v)
    r2 <- summary(lm(as.formula(paste(v, "~", paste(others, collapse = "+"))),
                     data = X))$r.squared
    1 / (1 - r2)
  }, numeric(1))
}

vif_vals <- vif_from_lm(df, c("age", "diabetes", "heart_failure", "copd", "hypertension", "los_gt7"))
vif_data <- tibble(Variable = names(vif_vals), VIF = round(unname(vif_vals), 2))
cat("Variance Inflation Factors:\n")
```

## 5. Model Evaluation — ROC, AUC, Calibration


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Predicted probabilities
df$pred_prob <- predict(model_multi, type = "response")

# ── ROC curve ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
roc_obj <- pROC::roc(df$readmitted_30, df$pred_prob, quiet = TRUE)
auc <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))
coords_youden <- pROC::coords(roc_obj, "best", ret = c("threshold", "specificity", "sensitivity"),
                              best.method = "youden")
opt_thr <- as.numeric(coords_youden$threshold[1])
opt_fpr <- 1 - as.numeric(coords_youden$specificity[1])
opt_tpr <- as.numeric(coords_youden$sensitivity[1])

roc_df <- tibble(fpr = 1 - roc_obj$specificities, tpr = roc_obj$sensitivities)

p_roc <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), fill = "#2563EB", alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1E3A8A", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = opt_fpr, y = opt_tpr), colour = "#DC2626", size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "1 - Specificity (FPR)", y = "Sensitivity (TPR)",
    title = "A  ROC Curve",
    subtitle = sprintf("AUC = %.3f; optimal threshold = %.2f", auc, opt_thr)
  ) +
  coord_equal()

# ── Calibration plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
calib_df <- tibble(y = df$readmitted_30, p = df$pred_prob) |>
  mutate(bin = ntile(p, 10)) |>
  group_by(bin) |>
  summarise(prob_pred = mean(p), prob_true = mean(y), .groups = "drop")
brier <- mean((df$readmitted_30 - df$pred_prob)^2)

p_cal <- ggplot(calib_df, aes(prob_pred, prob_true)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(colour = "#DC2626", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = "#DC2626", size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean predicted probability", y = "Fraction of positives",
    title = "B  Calibration Plot (points close to diagonal = well-calibrated)"
  ) +
  annotate("label", x = 0.05, y = 0.92, hjust = 0,
           label = sprintf("Brier score = %.3f", brier), size = 3.2)

# ── Precision-Recall curve ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ord <- order(df$pred_prob, decreasing = TRUE)
y_ord <- df$readmitted_30[ord]
tp <- cumsum(y_ord); fp <- cumsum(1 - y_ord)
prec <- tp / (tp + fp)
rec  <- tp / sum(df$readmitted_30)
ap <- sum(diff(c(0, rec)) * prec[-1], na.rm = TRUE)
```

## 6. Hosmer-Lemeshow Goodness-of-Fit


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hosmer_lemeshow <- function(y_true, y_pred, n_groups = 10) {
  # Hosmer-Lemeshow test for logistic regression calibration.
  df_hl <- tibble(y = y_true, p = y_pred) |>
    mutate(decile = ntile(p, n_groups))
  grouped <- df_hl |>
    group_by(decile) |>
    summarise(
      obs_pos = sum(y),
      obs_neg = sum(y == 0),
      exp_pos = sum(p),
      exp_neg = sum(1 - p),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  hl_stat <- sum((grouped$obs_pos - grouped$exp_pos)^2 / grouped$exp_pos +
                   (grouped$obs_neg - grouped$exp_neg)^2 / grouped$exp_neg)
  p_val <- 1 - pchisq(hl_stat, df = n_groups - 2)
  list(stat = hl_stat, p = p_val)
}

hl <- hosmer_lemeshow(df$readmitted_30, df$pred_prob)
cat("Hosmer-Lemeshow test:\n")
```
